issue_context.title: Don't use System.Linq.Expressions in ActivatorUtilities.CreateFactory with AOT
issue_context.body:
`ActivatorUtilities.CreateFactory` uses compiled expressions to generate a high-performance factory on CoreCLR:

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/007df054a526ed9e3dc70b43bfa330943bd4816a/src/libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.Abstractions/src/ActivatorUtilities.cs#L126-L137

NativeAOT doesn't support compiled expressions. Expressions is now a negative:
* Expressions are interpreted, reducing performance compared to standard .NET reflection.
* System.Linq.Expressions usage increases app size

`CreateFactory` should check for `RuntimeFeature.IsDynamicCodeSupported` and provide a delegate that uses standard .NET reflection when dynamic code isn't supported.

For example:

https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/4d75ee9a7fbad112e29b8a1d77c7d96965f62b40/src/Shared/PropertyHelper/PropertyHelper.cs#L215-L243

review_comments:
(nit) we are losing coverage here on platforms that don't support RemoteExecutor (WASM, Mobile, etc).

Maybe keep the existing test method and add a new single test that does the same thing when `IsDynamicCodeSupported=false`.

The expression-based implementation calls Expression.Convert on the argument: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/1bc528df807b3ed0c39143cbaab89b852a77b5a6/src/libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.Abstractions/src/ActivatorUtilities.cs#L278

Are these conversions unnecessary here?
I don't think so. When `ConstructorInfo.Invoke` is called with an array of arguments, doesn't it handle that for you?

Yes, reflection `Invoke` does a number of bespoke conversions. The set of conversions done by reflection `Invoke` is different (neither subset or superset) from the set of conversions done by `Expression.Convert`.

I think it is very hard to make these implementations equal with the current reflection `Invoke`. I would ignore the problem for now and come back to it once we get to work on the new fast reflection Invoke APIs.
Is there a meaningful difference between HasDefaultValue==true vs false when DefaultValue is null?  I'm wondering if HasDefaultValue could essentially just be => DefaultValue is not null.
